variants.title: Turn a seed into evidence
variants.context: An adversarial case pairs a clean seed with a bounded attack, a validity decision, and an observed consequence. Validity comes before failure: a changed input counts only when it preserves the tested intent or expected label and stays inside the threat model.
variants.prompt: A robustness campaign starts from a labeled corpus. Put the steps for one case in order.

items.text: Record robust accuracy, attack success, severity, queries used, and results by slice.
Keep the case only if its expected result is trusted, and record whether the system is initially correct.
Check intent, expected label, fluency, and policy equivalence, with independent review where needed.
Version the valid failure with its defense, judge policy, and model artifacts for repeat testing.
Apply a named attack family under fixed query, edit, time, and restart limits.

variants.hint: One check decides whether a broken case counts as a model failure at all.
variants.explanation: Validity is judged before the consequence is scored, so an attack that changed the task never enters the denominator.

variants.title: Turn a seed into evidence
variants.context: An adversarial case pairs a clean seed with a bounded attack, a validity decision, and an observed consequence. Validity comes before failure: a changed input counts only when it preserves the tested intent or expected label and stays inside the threat model.
variants.prompt: An attack rewrites a sentence and the system now answers differently. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Confirm the rewrite came from the declared family and stayed inside its edit and query caps.
Store the valid failure as a regression bound to this target, attack, and judge version.
Confirm the original sentence had a trusted label and the system answered it correctly.
Decide whether the rewrite preserved the intent and the expected label before calling it a failure.
Score the consequence with its severity, the queries it consumed, and the slice it belongs to.

variants.hint: A different answer to a different question is not a robustness result.
variants.explanation: The invariant is validity before failure, so a rewrite that changed the task is reported as an attack-generation failure.

variants.title: Turn a seed into evidence
variants.context: An adversarial case pairs a clean seed with a bounded attack, a validity decision, and an observed consequence. Validity comes before failure: a changed input counts only when it preserves the tested intent or expected label and stays inside the threat model.
variants.prompt: An attack run hits its query cap without succeeding. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Score the case as defended at that budget and note the exhaustion beside the result.
Keep the run in the store so a later budget increase can be compared against it.
Review any candidate it produced for semantic and label validity before discarding the run.
Record that the run exhausted its declared query budget rather than stopping early.
Verify the seed was one the system originally handled correctly.

variants.hint: An exhausted budget and an early stop are not the same observation.
variants.explanation: Query exhaustion is reported separately, because treating it as a defense hides how much effort the search required.

variants.title: Run the evaluation pipeline
variants.context: The pipeline separates generation from judgment: a versioned seed corpus feeds bounded attack workers, an independent validity review combines deterministic checks, calibrated judges, and sampled human adjudication, a scorer computes curves and slices, and a release store preserves valid failures and gate outcomes.
variants.prompt: A team is building the offline robustness pipeline. Put its stages in order.

items.text: Combine deterministic checks, calibrated semantic judges, and sampled human adjudication.
Compute curves, attack yield, uncertainty, severity, and results by protected slice.
Run isolated attack families with per-case query, time, and restart budgets.
Store expected outputs, risk slices, provenance, and clean target results in a versioned corpus.
Preserve valid failures, gate outcomes, owners, exceptions, and approved model artifacts.

variants.hint: Which stage must not be performed by the model under test?
variants.explanation: Separating generation from validity review is what stops a system from generating, judging, and approving its own evidence.

variants.title: Run the evaluation pipeline
variants.context: The pipeline separates generation from judgment: a versioned seed corpus feeds bounded attack workers, an independent validity review combines deterministic checks, calibrated judges, and sampled human adjudication, a scorer computes curves and slices, and a release store preserves valid failures and gate outcomes.
variants.prompt: A new attack family is added to an existing pipeline. Put the work in order.

items.text: Extend the validity rules to the transformations the family produces and sample them for review.
Recompute the curve and slice results with the new family reported as its own denominator.
Add its valid failures to the regression store with the versions that produced them.
Give the new family its own isolated worker with declared query, time, and restart caps.
Pin the seed slices the new family will run against and their recorded clean results.

variants.hint: A new transformation may need a new validity rule.
variants.explanation: Each family carries its own budget, validity rule, and denominator, so its yield can be read without diluting the others.

variants.title: Run the evaluation pipeline
variants.context: The pipeline separates generation from judgment: a versioned seed corpus feeds bounded attack workers, an independent validity review combines deterministic checks, calibrated judges, and sampled human adjudication, a scorer computes curves and slices, and a release store preserves valid failures and gate outcomes.
variants.prompt: A tokenizer change lands and every stored result is now suspect. Put the revalidation in order.

items.text: Revalidate the generated candidates rather than reusing the previous validity decisions.
Update the regression store so the release decision points at the current artifacts.
Rerun the attack workers, since edit budgets and candidates depend on tokenization.
Recompute the robustness curve and slices against the newly measured baseline.
Reload the seed corpus and recompute the clean target results under the new tokenizer.

variants.hint: The baseline moved, so what can still be reused?
variants.explanation: Robustness is evidence about a versioned system, so a tokenizer change invalidates the baseline, the attacks, and the validity labels together.

variants.title: Keep the denominator honest
variants.context: Robustness numbers only mean something with their denominator. Clean accuracy is measured on labeled cases, validity is measured on the attacks generated from clean-correct seeds, and attack success and robust accuracy are measured on the valid adversarial cases alone.
variants.prompt: An evaluation starts from 1,200 labeled cases. The system is correct on 1,080 of them, 900 of those attacks pass validity review, and 225 valid attacks cause the target failure. What is robust accuracy on the valid adversarial set, in percent?
variants.hint: Which set does robust accuracy describe?
variants.explanation: 675 of the 900 valid adversarial cases survive the attack, which is 75 percent robust accuracy.

mistakes.feedback: That reports the attack success rate rather than robust accuracy.
That divides the 675 survivors by the 1,080 clean-correct seeds instead of the 900 valid attacks.

variants.title: Keep the denominator honest
variants.context: Robustness numbers only mean something with their denominator. Clean accuracy is measured on labeled cases, validity is measured on the attacks generated from clean-correct seeds, and attack success and robust accuracy are measured on the valid adversarial cases alone.
variants.prompt: An evaluation starts from 2,000 labeled cases. The system is correct on 1,600 of them, 1,200 of those attacks pass validity review, and 180 valid attacks cause the target failure. What is the valid attack success rate, in percent?
variants.hint: Only attacks that survived validity review can succeed or fail.
variants.explanation: 180 successes over 1,200 valid adversarial cases is a 15 percent attack success rate.

mistakes.feedback: That divides by the 1,600 clean-correct seeds instead of the 1,200 valid attacks.
That reports robust accuracy rather than attack success rate.

variants.title: Keep the denominator honest
variants.context: Robustness numbers only mean something with their denominator. Clean accuracy is measured on labeled cases, validity is measured on the attacks generated from clean-correct seeds, and attack success and robust accuracy are measured on the valid adversarial cases alone.
variants.prompt: An evaluation starts from 1,000 labeled cases. Attacks are generated from the 950 seeds the system answered correctly, and 760 candidates pass semantic and label review. What is the semantic-validity rate, in percent?
variants.hint: Validity is measured on the attacks that were actually generated.
variants.explanation: 760 of the 950 generated candidates pass review, an 80 percent validity rate that falls under the 85 percent floor.

mistakes.feedback: That divides by all 1,000 labeled cases instead of the 950 seeds that produced attacks.
That reports the invalid share rather than the validity rate.

variants.title: Apply the robustness gate
variants.context: The release gate reads several independent conditions: at least 85 percent of generated candidates pass semantic and label review, robust accuracy holds at or above its floor at every declared budget point with no critical slice below its own floor, and clean quality stays inside the allowed regression budget.
variants.prompt: Robust accuracy is 88 percent at a 50-query budget and 61 percent at the declared 400-query budget, against a 75 percent floor. What follows?
options: Accept it, and report the average of the two budget points as the headline.
Reject the claim, because the floor has to hold at every declared budget point.
Accept it, because the low-budget result shows the defense working as designed.
optionFeedback: Averaging across budgets hides the point at which the defense actually fails.
A bounded attacker with the declared budget already drops the system below its floor.
A low-budget result alone overstates robustness, which is why the curve is published.
variants.hint: The gate names budget points, not one number.
variants.explanation: Robustness is reported across attack effort, so a floor that fails at the declared budget fails the gate.

variants.title: Apply the robustness gate
variants.context: The release gate reads several independent conditions: at least 85 percent of generated candidates pass semantic and label review, robust accuracy holds at or above its floor at every declared budget point with no critical slice below its own floor, and clean quality stays inside the allowed regression budget.
variants.prompt: Overall robust accuracy holds above its floor at every budget point, but a critical medical slice falls below its own floor. What follows?
options: Release, because the overall curve stayed above the declared floor.
Release to a canary and watch the medical slice under real traffic.
Block, because critical slices carry floors that are gated separately.
optionFeedback: The overall curve is one condition, and the slice floor failed independently of it.
Monitoring does not replace a floor that was declared before the results arrived.
Slice floors exist so an average across easy slices cannot absorb a critical failure.
variants.hint: Ask which conditions the gate requires at the same time.
variants.explanation: Critical slices are gated separately instead of being averaged away, since the consequence differs by slice.

variants.title: Apply the robustness gate
variants.context: The release gate reads several independent conditions: at least 85 percent of generated candidates pass semantic and label review, robust accuracy holds at or above its floor at every declared budget point with no critical slice below its own floor, and clean quality stays inside the allowed regression budget.
variants.prompt: A defense raises robust accuracy above the floor, but clean task accuracy drops six points past the allowed regression budget. What follows?
options: Release, because the robustness improvement is what the gate was measuring.
Release, and treat the clean regression as a separate quality workstream.
Block, because clean and robust quality are reported and gated together.
optionFeedback: Robust numbers can rise simply because the baseline fell, which the clean gate detects.
Deferring the regression lets the candidate ship with a failure the gate already caught.
A defense that damages the baseline is not a robustness win, so both metrics are read together.
variants.hint: What happens to robust accuracy when the baseline itself gets worse?
variants.explanation: Clean and robust metrics are reported together so a defense cannot hide behind a damaged baseline.

variants.title: Name the defense failure
variants.context: Defense failures repeat in recognizable shapes: benchmark overfitting to public attack templates, invalid perturbations accepted by a weak semantic judge, gradient masking or detector artifacts that make weak attacks look unsuccessful, clean-quality regression, and system-boundary substitution when a model defense is credited for an authorization problem.
variants.prompt: After a new input filter, one attack family stops succeeding entirely, but a different search method at a higher budget still finds valid failures. What is the failure?
options: Invalid perturbations, so audit the semantic judge for candidates that changed intent.
Gradient masking or a detector artifact, so raise the budget and vary the search.
Benchmark overfitting, so keep hidden attacks and rotate the transformations used.
optionFeedback: The successful candidates were valid, so the judge is not what failed.
A weak attack looking unsuccessful because input handling broke is exactly this pattern.
The attacks here are not public templates; a different search still succeeds.
variants.hint: Did the system get stronger, or did one attack get weaker?
variants.explanation: When one search method stalls while another succeeds, the optimization was obstructed rather than the model being robust.

variants.title: Name the defense failure
variants.context: Defense failures repeat in recognizable shapes: benchmark overfitting to public attack templates, invalid perturbations accepted by a weak semantic judge, gradient masking or detector artifacts that make weak attacks look unsuccessful, clean-quality regression, and system-boundary substitution when a model defense is credited for an authorization problem.
variants.prompt: A defense scores very well on the public attack set it was tuned against, then fails on a held-out adaptive suite. What is the failure?
options: System-boundary substitution, so trace the attack to its accountable control owner.
Benchmark overfitting, so keep hidden attacks and rotate transformations.
Clean-quality regression, so report baseline and robust metrics side by side.
optionFeedback: The failure is a model behavior, not a control credited to the wrong owner.
Learning the public templates is not the same as resisting an adaptive attacker.
Nothing here says ordinary task quality moved; the held-out attacks are what failed.
variants.hint: What separates the set it passed from the set it failed?
variants.explanation: Attack generation and defense tuning must not share every case, which is why a held-out adaptive suite exists.

variants.title: Name the defense failure
variants.context: Defense failures repeat in recognizable shapes: benchmark overfitting to public attack templates, invalid perturbations accepted by a weak semantic judge, gradient masking or detector artifacts that make weak attacks look unsuccessful, clean-quality regression, and system-boundary substitution when a model defense is credited for an authorization problem.
variants.prompt: Adversarial training is credited for stopping a retrieved document that overrode trusted instructions and reached private context. What is the failure?
options: Invalid perturbations, since the retrieved document changed the tested intent.
System-boundary substitution, since this needs authorization and trust isolation.
Gradient masking, since the attack only appears unsuccessful under a weak search.
optionFeedback: The document is a genuine attack path, not an invalid perturbation of a seed.
Model robustness cannot enforce authorization, so the control owner here is the wrong one.
Nothing suggests the search was obstructed; the boundary itself is the issue.
variants.hint: Which control would actually have to hold for this path to be closed?
variants.explanation: Trust and authorization controls cannot be replaced by model robustness, so the attack is traced to the protected asset and its owner.
